change.author: Alan

findings.title: Crash when the event has no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` sets the value to `undefined` when the user has no destination calendar. `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` in that case, and other callers set it to `[]`. Line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, so whenever the location is Google Meet, `EventManager.create` throws a TypeError for any user with no destination calendar set. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, so this case fell back to Cal Video. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Organization slug logic is inverted
findings.body: The old code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug was set right away only when team billing was off, and with billing on it went into `requestedSlug` until payment. The new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` reverses that. With billing on, the org gets its slug before anyone pays. With billing off, self-hosted orgs never get a slug at all. This change has nothing to do with destination calendars. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`.

findings.title: Team members' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` (line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so a COLLECTIVE booking writes to none of the members' calendars even though they have destination calendars. Nothing is shown to anyone. Fall back to `[]` on line 1067, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when the value is null.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: Before, non-calendar results stored `result.credentialId`. Now they store `undefined`, so `_video` booking references are saved with no credentialId. `handleCancelBooking.ts:722-741` relies on `reference.credentialId` to load the credential and call `updateMeeting` when one seat is cancelled. Without it, the video meeting is silently left out of the update. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup can never match
findings.body: The `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it then looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (null or undefined), so it always returns undefined. The old fallback to the destination calendar's `externalId` is gone. Updates (and deletes, line 317) for references with no `externalCalendarId` now go to the default calendar instead of the event's destination calendar, and Google will return 404 for events that live elsewhere. The fallback create path at `EventManager.ts:380` makes this worse: it calls `createEvent(c, event)` with no externalId, so new references there also have no `externalCalendarId`. Fall back to the destination entry whose `credentialId` matches this service's credential, or to the first entry.

findings.title: References from the fallback path no longer store externalCalendarId
findings.body: Before, `externalCalendarId` came from `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. It now comes from `result.externalId`, which `CalendarManager.createEvent` only fills when the third argument is passed. This branch (destination with no credentialId) does not pass it, so these references are saved with `externalCalendarId` undefined. Later updates and deletes then fall back to the primary calendar (see the Google update/delete finding). Pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

findings.title: Non-Google services always use the main host's calendar ID
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` now calls `createEvent` once per collective member's credential. Office 365 (here), Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128`) and CalDAV (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156`) still read `destinationCalendar[0]`, which is the organizer's calendar. A member's Outlook credential will POST to `/me/calendars/<organizer's id>/events`, which fails or picks the wrong calendar. A member's CalDAV credential filters out all of its own calendars, so no event is created. Only Google uses the `credentialId` it is given. These services should also pick the entry whose `credentialId` matches their own credential.

findings.title: Recurring deletion runs again for every calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-series branch is now inside the loop over references, so it deletes every remaining occurrence across all of the user's calendar credentials once per reference. With N calendar references, each delete is sent N times. The repeat calls fail (already deleted), and those errors are only logged. Move the recurring branch out of the loop.

contracts.action: Load missing credentials from the DB for team-member destination calendars and video reference handling
contracts.equivalent_path: handleCancelBooking seat path loads credentials by reference.credentialId
contracts.before_after: Video references used to keep result.credentialId; now they keep undefined
contracts.visible_effect: When a seat is cancelled, the video meeting is not updated
contracts.failure_mode: Silent: the reference has no credentialId, so the update is skipped

summary: The change turns destinationCalendar into an array so collective events can be written to every member's calendar. Main problems: a TypeError when the location is Google Meet and there is no destination calendar, an unrelated inversion of the org slug billing logic, members' calendars dropped when the organizer has none, lost credentialId on video references, a Google update/delete fallback that can never match, and non-Google services that always use the organizer's calendar ID.
